summary: Independent runtime audit found that the universal-worker validator does not bind claim.write_scope to the canonical queue opportunity, prefers claim.write_scope when validating attempted paths, does not independently protect global authority-owner paths, and has no equivalent fail-closed privacy/publication check. No protected owner mutation or private-data leak was observed; findings are canary blockers before production /w promotion.

acceptance_evidence.route_changing_falsification: A worker-controlled claim.write_scope can be broader than canonical opportunity.write_scope; current envelope validation prefers the claim scope for attempted_paths and does not independently resolve canonical opportunity provenance.
acceptance_evidence.privacy_gap: Declared public-artifact privacy exclusions have no corresponding universal-worker envelope validation step in the inspected kernel.
acceptance_evidence.concurrent_evidence_note: A separate canary-evidence hardening worker added an out-of-scope WRITE_SET fixture during this audit. That is complementary evidence work; it does not by itself demonstrate canonical queue-scope binding when the declared scope itself is worker-controlled.

candidate_next_work.activation: After O-SWARM-KERNEL-IMPLEMENT-V1 returns and is dispositioned, unless its durable return already closes AUTH-01/AUTH-02/PRIV-01 with negative tests.
candidate_next_work.mission: Bind validation to a trusted canonical opportunity ref/hash, derive or subset-check claim scope, independently block protected authority-owner paths for universal workers, and add fail-closed public-artifact privacy/provenance validation with negative tests.
